correctness.rationale: Model is a bounded trace-class Lindblad generator plus Poisson reset. Exponential reset contraction gives a unique stationary state; a site-monitoring renewal with exact Bessel squared free kernel yields the normalized Fourier formula. Algebraically separating the rational simple pole from the square-root branch and evaluating the Fourier cut gives the exact positive integral, checked independently against quadrature and finite-ring Liouvillians. Watson’s lemma proves distinct fixed-rate prefactors, and dominated convergence on the rescaled branch integral plus quadratic pole–edge separation yields the erfc crossover for all sequences gamma_m sqrt(m/C_gamma)→u≥0. Boundary gamma=0, symmetry, variance and r,h restrictions are explicitly treated. The checker is corroborative, not proof of infinite-volume assertions.

value.rationale: For fixed positive reset rate the stationary site distribution has a physically interpretable spatial-decay tail. The sharp change of the algebraic prefactor at exactly zero dephasing creates a nonuniform small-noise limit, and its distance scale proportional to gamma^{-2} is a measurable crossover. Exact positive pole/branch decomposition and universal erfc scaling resolve a motivated singular boundary of quantum-to-classical transport, going beyond a routine stationary resolvent computation. The result is analytically self-contained for an infinite natural network; extensions to disorder or finite observation time remain open.
